- File: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/escalation-judge.md
  Line or code reference: Step 4, line 37 ("For a security stop the stage still writes no security patch itself ... the narrower fix is ... a note on the follow-up issues for their own pipeline") combined with Step 8, line 53 (budget/descope hand-on) and implement-plan-claude.md line 332 ("It runs one more round past the cap and applies the narrower fix the entry names")
  Problem: For a `security-followup-unmerged` stop, the judge may name "a note on the follow-up issues for their own pipeline" as the narrower fix for a `budget` choice. But the budget stage that re-runs the security pass (step 9 of implement-plan-claude) only re-dispatches the audit — the procedure does not instruct the budget stage session to post that note on the follow-up issues before re-dispatching. The instruction "applies the narrower fix the entry names" is generic; step 9 itself only dispatches the audit workflow and reads its result. If the budget stage does not post the note, the audit re-dispatches against the same blocked/unmerged follow-up, reports the same finding, and fires `security-followup-unmerged` again with the same fingerprint. The `budget` choice is now used for that failure, leaving only `descope` or `close` — the grant was spent without applying the remedy it named.
  Why it fails at runtime: The budget stage session for a security stop re-runs step 9 (security pass), which re-dispatches `security-audit.yml`. The audit re-checks the follow-up issues. A blocked or unmerged follow-up is still blocked or unmerged, so the audit reports `findings` above 0 (or the follow-up is still closed without `ai:merged`), the pass is not clean, and the stop fires again with the same fingerprint. The `budget` grant was consumed without effect.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Problem: The procedure defines a blocked-and-notify path for `allowed` failures (step 3: "Exit 2 or any other non-zero exit is not a choice: ... leave `Status: BLOCKED` for a human, send one `PushNotification` ... and end the turn") but not for non-zero exits from `fingerprint` (step 2) or `record` (step 5). Step 0 (preflight) has already deleted the safety-net and hand-back triggers. If `fingerprint` exits 1 (e.g., a PR-scoped stop without `pr` evidence, or an unknown stop id) or `record` exits 1 (e.g., a reason holding `<!--`, evidence mismatch, used choice), the judge has no defined recovery path: no instruction to send a `PushNotification`, no instruction to leave `Status: BLOCKED` for a human, no instruction to end the turn. The Never list at line 76 only mentions steps 1 and 3 as the paths that end at BLOCKED without a choice, confirming steps 2 and 5 are uncovered.
  Why it fails at runtime: If `fingerprint` fails, step 3 cannot run (no fingerprint to pass to `allowed`). If `record` fails, step 6 cannot run (no `ES-<n>` line to post). In either case the safety net has been deleted, so the project stalls silently if the judge does not improvise a notification. An unattended session with no defined recovery path and no safety net leaves the project blocked without operator awareness.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
